results.title: Lee touts new deposit system as effective in curbing illegal fishing by Chinese vessels
results.content: President Lee Jae Myung on Thursday touted a tightened deposit system introduced by the Coast Guard, saying it has been significantly effective in curbing illegal fishing by Chinese vessels. Lee made the remarks in a post on his X account, sharing a news report that an increasing number of Chinese fishermen have given up their boats and abandoned illegal operations due to the financial burden since the Coast Guard began requiring deposits of up to 1.5 billion won ($1.1 million) in May from Chinese vessels caught fishing illegally. The Coast Guard requires the deposits in exchange for the release of Chinese vessels caught fishing illegally and their crew members. Previously, the maximum deposit was capped at 300 million won. results.title: Stunning stars, disappointing styling: Lee Na-young, Kim Tae-hee, Son Ye-jin
results.content: Actress Lee Na-young's disappointing styling has drawn attention, prompting renewed scrutiny of the red-carpet looks of Kim Tae-hee and Son Ye-jin, whose fashion choices at public events have previously sparked comments that their stylists seemed to be working against them. Lee attended a photo call for an Italian jewelry brand at Cove the Jangchung in Seoul on Tuesday. She paired a white suit with a gold necklace and statement rings, creating an elegant look. However, the loose-fitting suit, which obscured her slender figure, left some viewers disappointed. Her hairstyle also divided opinions. Deeply parted hair with thick waves cascading over one cheek created a classic look, but some found it a little heavy and stifling. results.title: Defense minister calls for easing tension with Russia after air defense zone entry
results.content: Defense Minister Kang Shin-chul on Thursday called for efforts to ease tensions with Russia, after Russian warplanes flew into Korea's air defense zone and almost breached its territorial airspace earlier this week. Two Russian Tu-160 supersonic strategic bombers and two other fighter jets entered Korea's air defense identification zone (KADIZ) in the East Sea early Tuesday. They came within about 1 kilometer of the airspace over Ulleung Island off the east coast, prompting the Korean Air Force to scramble fighter jets in response. Seoul has lodged a strong protest with the Russians over their repeated unannounced and unauthorized entry into KADIZ. "I believe we need to make efforts to ease tensions at this point," Kang said during a parliamentary session. "While we maintain communication channels with Russia, I believe we should do more." results.title: Korea secures final victory in ISDS case brought by Iran's Dayyani family
results.content: The Korean government has secured a final victory in the second investor-state dispute settlement (ISDS) arbitration brought by six members of Iran's Dayyani family, the justice ministry said Thursday. The ministry said the dismissal of the entire 770 billion won ($573 million) claim has become final, as the Dayyani family did not file a challenge with a British court to set aside the second ISDS arbitral award within the statutory deadline. As a result, the Korean government is not only free from any obligation to pay the claimed amount but will also recover 4.8 billion won in legal costs, it said. The case traces back to 2015, when the Dayyanis, a major shareholder of Entekhab Industrial Group, filed for arbitration after Korea's state-run Korea Asset Management canceled a contract to sell a major stake in Daewoo Electronics to Entekhab in 2011. results.title: Unification minister nominee favors small steps over high-level talks with N. Korea
results.content: Unification Minister nominee Hong Ihk-pyo said Thursday that Seoul should break the deadlock with Pyongyang through small, practical steps rather than a push for high-level talks. “Given the current state of inter-Korean relations and the situation on the Korean Peninsula, I think it might be better to start with smaller and more practical steps rather than pursue high-level talks,” Hong said during a doorstep interview in Seoul. Hong, a former presidential secretary and three-term lawmaker, was nominated Monday as part of President Lee Jae Myung's reshuffle of key security posts, a move widely read as an effort to steady ties with Washington after friction over intelligence sharing during Chung Dong-young's tenure. results.title: Exhibition in Seoul explores cultural roots of Gwangcheon 'gim'
results.content: As Korean food gains fans worldwide, "gim," or dried seaweed, has moved from everyday Korean tables to fine dining menus, becoming one of the country’s hottest exports. To highlight the history and culinary versatility behind one of the country’s most recognized seaweed-producing regions, Hongseong County in South Chungcheong Province recently opened a pop-up exhibition titled “Hongseong Seafood Market, Do You Know Gim?” in Seoul. The exhibition focuses on Gwangcheon, a town in Hongseong where more than 40 companies produce hundreds of varieties of seasoned gim. While “Gwangcheon gim” is widely known among consumers, organizers said many people mistakenly view it as a single commercial brand rather than a regional industry built over decades. results.title: Kim Do-yeong joins elite company with 2nd career KBO MVP award
results.content: Just five years into his career in the Korea Baseball Organization (KBO), Kia Tigers third baseman Kim Do-yeong has already made plenty of history with his numerous feats. On Thursday, the 23-year-old etched himself into the record books once again by capturing his second career MVP award. Kim collected 80 out of 136 votes from the media for the honor, with Doosan Bears pitcher Gwak Been finishing as a distant runner-up with 34 votes. Kim, who won his first MVP honor in 2024, is now the sixth player to win the league's highest individual honor multiple times. Former Samsung Lions great Lee Seung-yuop leads the way as the five-time winner, and former Tigers ace Sun Dong-yol won three MVPs. Three other former players, Kim Sung-han, Jang Jong-hoon and Park Byung-ho, each won two MVP awards. results.title: PPP refuses to recommend special counsel candidate to probe alleged fabricated indictments
results.content: Two candidates were recommended by the ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK) and a minor opposition party Thursday to lead a special counsel probe into allegations of fabricated indictments against President Lee Jae Myung, while the main opposition People Power Party (PPP) refused to make a recommendation. A special counsel bill was passed by the National Assembly earlier this month and approved by the Cabinet last week, calling for an independent counsel to investigate suspicions that the prosecution under former President Yoon Suk Yeol fabricated evidence or induced false testimonies to build cases against then opposition leader Lee and others. The new special prosecutor is to be chosen by President Lee from among three candidates recommended by the DPK, the PPP and the minor Rebuilding Korea Party. results.title: FM Cho reaffirms Korea's non-involvement stance on US-Iran war in call with Iranian counterpart
results.content: Foreign Minister Cho Hyun on Thursday explained Korea's plans to expand the operational area of its naval unit near the Strait of Hormuz and reaffirmed its non-involvement stance on the U.S.-Iran war during phone talks with his Iranian counterpart, the foreign ministry said. Cho held talks with Iranian Foreign Minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi to discuss the latest developments in the Middle East, bilateral relations and the protection of Korean nationals abroad, according to the ministry. The talks came as the National Assembly's defense committee approved a motion to extend the deployment of the anti-piracy Cheonghae unit and expand its operational area from waters off Somalia to waters south of Oman, closer to the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial shipping route that has effectively been choked off amid the ongoing war. results.title: Real household income falls despite chip export boom
results.content: Real household income in Korea fell for the first time in 10 quarters in the third quarter, according to data released Thursday by the Ministry of Data and Statistics. The decline came even as the economy grew 3.4 percent in the quarter, buoyed by a semiconductor boom, and was expected to expand in the high 3 percent range this year. The benefits of economic growth were uneven across households. Lower-income families earned less from work and received less in transfers while facing higher interest payments, further widening the income gap. Average monthly household income rose 0.8 percent from a year earlier to 5.48 million won ($4,080), the data showed. Adjusted for inflation, however, it fell 2.1 percent, the first decline since the first quarter of 2024, when real household income fell 1.6 percent. results.title: KOSPI edges up despite BOK rate hike
results.content: The benchmark KOSPI edged up 0.29 percent Thursday despite the central bank’s rate hike, with chipmakers leading the rebound. The index recouped only a fraction of its loss of more than 6 percent in the previous session. The benchmark KOSPI closed at 4,711.21 after opening 1.01 percent higher at 4,745.10. The index briefly climbed above the 4,800-mark but gave up most of its gains toward the close. Institutional investors led the buying, purchasing a net 750.9 billion won ($560 million), while foreign investors and retail investors recorded net sales of 113.6 billion won and 1.04 trillion won, respectively. Samsung Electronics rose 0.35 percent to close at 171,300 won, while SK hynix gained 2.23 percent to finish at 1,053,000 won. results.title: Real estate developer-led consortium expresses intent to acquire troubled retailer Homeplus: sources
results.content: A consortium led by a real estate developer is reportedly pursuing the acquisition of the troubled discount store chain Homeplus, industry sources said Thursday. The consortium, comprised of a real estate developer and a logistics company, has submitted a letter of intent (LOI) to purchase the entire retail chain, according to sources. The lead underwriter is said to be monitoring the market situation while being open to non-binding offers from other bidders, they added. In September, the Seoul Bankruptcy Court approved a corporate rehabilitation plan for Homeplus, wholly owned by private equity firm MBK Partners. But the discount store chain has been struggling to repay its debts amounting to 1.3 trillion won ($968.3 million) due to a liquidity crunch. results.title: Korea challenges US claims of state-led overcapacity
results.content: Korea is pushing back against Washington's claim that its industrial policies are contributing to structural excess capacity in manufacturing, as a new U.S. tariff investigation raises concerns over whether support for domestic semiconductor production could face further trade pressure. The Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources said Thursday that it disagrees with much of the evidence cited by the U.S. Trade Representative (USTR), arguing that Korea's industrial policies are driven by market demand and companies' investment decisions rather than government efforts to expand production beyond actual demand. It emphasized that it would seek to preserve the 15 percent tariff ceiling agreed under last year’s bilateral trade deal. “There are substantial parts of the report cited by the USTR that we cannot agree with. results.title: Korea, Russia discuss KADIZ issue after Russian warplanes' close approach
results.content: The Korean foreign ministry held talks with a Russian Embassy official in Seoul on Thursday over the entry of Russian military aircraft into the country's air defense zone earlier this week, sources said. A minister-counselor-level diplomat from the Russian Embassy visited the ministry's headquarters earlier in the day, where the two sides discussed the entry of Russian military aircraft into the Korea Air Defense Identification Zone (KADIZ) and other pending issues, according to the diplomatic sources. On Tuesday, two Tu-160 strategic bombers, capable of carrying nuclear missiles, entered the KADIZ along with Su-35S and Su-30SM fighter jets, approaching to within 1 kilometer of the boundary of Korean airspace near Ulleung Island in the East Sea, according to military authorities here. results.title: Tigers superstar Kim Do-yeong claims 2nd KBO MVP award
results.content: Kim Do-yeong of the Kia Tigers captured his second career MVP award in Korean baseball Thursday on the strength of a bounceback season that immediately followed an injury-plagued campaign. The 23-year-old superstar received 80 out of 136 votes from members of the Korea Baseball Writers Association, beating out Doosan Bears starter Gwak Been, who had 34 votes, for the top individual honor in the Korea Baseball Organization (KBO). Kim led the KBO with 45 home runs and a .647 slugging percentage. He also ranked inside the top five in runs (120), RBIs (118), total bases (321), on-base percentage (.413) and on-base plus slugging (1.060). This year, Kim became the youngest player in league history to record at least 40 home runs, 100 RBIs and 100 runs scored. results.title: Eagles catcher Heo In-seo voted KBO's top rookie for 2026
results.content: Heo In-seo, the 23-year-old backstop for the Hanwha Eagles, was named the top rookie in Korean baseball for 2026 on Thursday. Heo collected 92 out of 136 votes from members of the Korea Baseball Writers Association to win the Rookie of the Year award in the Korea Baseball Organization (KBO) over SSG Landers pitcher Kim Min-jun, who received 20 votes. Heo is the fifth Eagles player to be voted the top rookie and the first catcher to win this award since Yang Eui-ji of the Doosan Bears in 2010. Heo led all eligible rookies with 20 home runs and 79 RBIs this year, while batting .283/.349/.472 in 130 games. "At the start of the season, I never imagined I would be able to win this award," Heo said. "All I wanted to do was just to stay with the club, even just as a backup. I am really grateful for this." results.title: Interior ministry to train local officials to prevent erroneous disaster alerts
results.content: The interior ministry said Thursday it will provide special training for local government officials responsible for issuing civil defense alerts to prevent the erroneous transmission of emergency disaster messages. The special training will take place for two days next week for about 170 officials from 16 metropolitan and provincial governments nationwide, the ministry said. The measure follows an incident on Tuesday, in which North Gyeongsang Province authorities sent an emergency alert to the East Sea island of Ulleung containing incorrect information, causing confusion among residents. At that time, several Russian warplanes briefly entered South Korea's air defense zone over the East Sea but the province's civil defense warning control center described them as aerial objects presumed to be North Korean aircraft in its emergency message sent to the island. results.content: The main entrance of Starbucks's N Seoul Tower branch, set to open Friday, is seen in this handout photo. The company's 15th special store in Korea is located on the fourth and fifth floors of the Seoul landmark on Mount Nam and incorporates key elements inspired by traditional Korean hanok architecture. The store offers exclusive drinks, including a latte made with scorched rice, a traditional Korean ingredient, and a cocktail inspired by makgeolli, a traditional Korean rice alcohol. results.title: [COVER STORY] Gov't weighs banning part-time work for int'l students lacking Korean proficiency
results.content: International students who fall short on Korean language requirements could face a complete ban on part-time work, even if when they were enrolled in English-taught programs. The Ministry of Justice is reviewing the measure, along with plans to shorten post-graduation stays for those with limited Korean proficiency. If implemented, the measures would make Korean language skills a key determinant of international students' ability to work and stay in the country. The proposed changes come as Korea reassesses its international student policy amid growing concerns that aggressive recruitment by universities — sometimes involving inducement of guaranteeing part-time work — may come at the expense of educational quality. results.title: North Korea's Kim stresses party discipline, loyalty in letter to grassroots leaders' conference
results.content: North Korean leader Kim Jong-un stressed the need to unify the ruling party's grassroots cells under a single ideology and will in a letter read at a meeting of cell secretaries of the Workers' Party of Korea (WPK), state media said Thursday. Kim "stressed the importance of consolidating all the Party cells into the ones of single ideology and will, steadfast in their revolutionary faith and obligation," according to the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA). Party cells refer to the party's most elementary units, consisting of five to 30 members. Jo Yong-won, a member of the Presidium of the Political Bureau and secretary for Organizational Affairs of the WPK Central Committee, delivered Kim's letter to the Seventh Conference of Cell Secretaries of the WPK. results.content: Jin and Hattie, a Korean-British couple who rose to fame through their YouTube channel with 10.1 million subscribers, have announced their divorce, saying they will continue to manage their social media platforms separately. Heo Jin-woo and Harriet Emily shared a lengthy statement Wednesday on their YouTube community page and social media accounts announcing their separation. results.content: Prime Minister Han Seong-sook expressed gratitude Thursday to test supervisors at last week's annual college entrance exam, saying they must have remained on edge throughout the test due to a series of measures added to prevent cheating and that the government will look for ways to minimize their burden next year. Thousands of additional personnel, usually school teachers, were mobilized to supervise the College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT), known as Suneung in Korean, to enforce a series of anti-cheating measures, including checking test-takers' glasses and clothing. "This year's Suneung was an unfamiliar experience for both students and teachers," Han said on X. results.title: A Chinese consumer advocate is stranded in South Korea as a crackdown in China targets campaigners
results.content: WASHINGTON — Chinese consumer rights advocate Wang Hai has spent three decades exposing counterfeit goods and seeking compensation for buyers. In recent months, he left China fearing he was a target of the authorities, but now he is stranded in South Korea with his family, facing possible deportation home. Wang, a well-known campaigner against counterfeit goods, said China invalidated his passport and South Korean authorities rejected his asylum. The United States also revoked his tourist visa, narrowing his options for leaving South Korea and deepening his fears of being sent back to China. results.title: New bills target stealth recording with AI glasses
results.content: Lawmakers of the ruling Democratic Party of Korea have proposed bills to stop people from secretly filming others with artificial intelligence (AI)-powered smart glasses, amid growing concern that wearable cameras are making illegal filming harder to detect. Rep. Lee Ju-hee and 18 DPK colleagues have submitted an amendment to the Information and Communications Network Act to require makers and importers of wearable cameras to include a recording indicator that people nearby can easily recognize. It is one of two bills in what the lawmaker calls the “Smart Glasses Illegal Filming Prevention Act,” introduced earlier this week. The other bill would also require individuals who film others with such devices to signal that they are recording. results.title: Integrated LCC headquarters to be based in Busan
results.content: The headquarters of the integrated low-cost carrier (LCC) formed through the merger of Air Busan, Jin Air and Air Seoul will be based in Busan, the city government said Thursday. Busan Mayor Chun Jae-soo and Hanjin Group Chairman Cho Won-tae reached the agreement during a meeting in Busan, paving the way for the launch of the integrated airline in March next year. The agreement follows close consultations between the city and Korean Air, with Hanjin Group making the decision in consideration of Busan's growth potential and the importance of balanced national development, according to the city government. The integration follows Korean Air's acquisition of Asiana Airlines, scheduled to be completed on Dec. 17. results.title: Law banning foreigners' political activity ruled unconstitutional
results.content: The Constitutional Court ruled Thursday that a provision of the Immigration Act imposing a general ban on political activity by foreign residents does not conform to the Constitution, with six of the nine judges agreeing. To prevent a legal vacuum, however, the court kept the clause in effect until it can be revised, no later than Dec. 31, 2028. The provision was introduced in 1977. A 2005 amendment added an exception for political activities permitted under other laws, but the general ban stayed in place. Violators can be ordered to halt the activity or leave the country and those without permanent resident status may face deportation. results.title: Scholars from 3 nations to discuss Ahn Jung-geun's legacy, missing remains
results.content: Scholars from Korea, China and Japan will gather Friday for an international academic conference commemorating Korean independence activist Ahn Jung-geun. The conference will be co-hosted by Kookmin University and the Korea-China Civilian Standing Committee for the Search for Ahn Jung-geun, with support from the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. The event, to be held at the Ahn Jung-geun Memorial Museum in Seoul, will focus on the theme “Korean, Chinese and Japanese Perspective on Ahn Jung-geun’s Martyrdom and Commemoration.” The conference will open with an address by Chung Sye-kyun, chairman of the Ahn Jung-geun Memorial Association, followed by remarks from Jung Tae-ho, co-chair of the National Assembly Caucus for the Exhumation and Repatriation of Ahn Jung-geun’s Remains. results.title: FM nominee says Korea-US alliance 'strong enough to overcome any difficulty'
results.content: Foreign Minister nominee Lim Woong-soon dismissed concerns about recent friction with Washington, Thursday, saying the alliance is resilient enough to weather any challenge. "The alliance has evolved over more than 70 years. Given that long history and the values and interests our two countries share, I believe the two can overcome any difficulty," Lim said during a doorstep interview in Seoul. "I don't think the Korea-U.S. alliance is so fragile that any particular issue could shake it." He also struck a balanced tone on relations with Beijing. “I believe both our alliance with the U.S. and our relationship with China are important to us. I don't think there is a single country that doesn't matter to South Korea.” His remarks came amid a strain in Seoul-Washington ties. results.title: HS Hyosung promotes 2 CEOs to presidents
results.content: HS Hyosung said Thursday it promoted Ahn Sung-hoon, CEO of HS Hyosung, and Seong Nak-yang, CEO of HS Hyosung Advanced Materials, from executive vice presidents to presidents in its 2027 executive reshuffle. Born in 1971, Ahn joined Hyosung Group in 2000 after a stint at global consulting firm Bain & Company. He spent nearly two decades at Hyosung Heavy Industries, serving as executive vice president overseeing its power systems business, before becoming HS Hyosung's inaugural CEO in 2024. The group credited him with stabilizing the organization and strengthening its business competitiveness following its launch. Seong previously served as CEO of Yahoo Korea and Doosan Glonet, as well as a global partner at McKinsey and Accenture and head of management innovation at Hyosung Group. results.title: US military confirms inactivation of Apache helicopter squadron in South Korea
results.content: The U.S. Forces Korea (USFK) confirmed Thursday that an Army aviation unit in South Korea has been inactivated, noting that the move does not change the United States' military force posture or commitment to the defense of the Asian ally.
